source.prompt: A team updated a Feishu Bitable single-select field by sending only a target list of option names; the API rebuilt every option with brand-new ids, and all existing data rows silently lost their references (values cleared). Return the one-line fix rule in answer: it must say to merge options by stable id — existing names keep their old id (pass the original object through), only genuinely new names get fresh ids continuing from max(existing id)+1 — and warn that rebuilding the list by name alone silently breaks every existing row reference. Put a reusable instruction for any id-referenced catalog update in reuse_advice.

transfer.prompt: You are updating an options catalog. Variables in scope: existing = list of {'id': int, 'name': str} dicts; target_names = list of desired names (keep those that exist, add those that do not, drop the rest). Return ONE Python expression in terms of existing and target_names that evaluates to the new options list of {'id','name'} dicts. Only stdlib builtins like max/enumerate/sorted; no lambda, no def, no imports.
